title: PNP-ACG warns public vs. bogus online followers, reviews
summary: The Philippine National Police's Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) on Wednesday warned the public to be cautious when purchasing items from online sellers this coming holiday season.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police's Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) on Wednesday warned the public to be cautious when purchasing items from online sellers this coming holiday season.
According to GMA News' Jun Veneracion, the PNP-ACG said that some online sellers allegedly buy online followers and reviews.

"Ang followers po ngayon ay hindi na po guarantee na 'yung account na 'yun ay totoo. Kasi 'yung mga followers ngayon ay nabibili na lang po, pati 'yung mga reviews gawa-gawa na lang din po," said PNP-ACG spokesperson Police Lieutenantt Colonel Zyrah Joy Cabal.
(Nowadays, having followers is no longer a guarantee that an account is real. Because followers today can simply be bought, and even the reviews are just fabricated.)
Since 2021, online selling scams have topped the ACG's list of cybercrime modus operandi.
In the ACG's report, 743 incidents of online selling scams were recorded from January to October this year.

"Sa ating mga buyers, pagtitignan ninyo po 'yung mga testimonials, mga reviews, pakisuyo po na tignan na rin po ang mga profile ng mga nagre-review na ito, para malaman ninyo kung legit nga talaga ang kanilang nire-review," Cabal added.

(To our buyers, when you look at testimonials and reviews, please also check the profiles of those leaving these reviews so you can find out if what they are reviewing is truly legitimate.) —Vince Angelo Ferreras/AOL, GMA News
